q: On which date did RBI release its guidelines for licensing payments banks?
explain: RBI published the payments bank licensing guidelines on 27 November 2014; in-principle approvals followed in August 2015.

q: Small finance banks were recommended by which committee on financial inclusion?
explain: The Nachiket Mor Committee on financial inclusion recommended niche banks such as small finance banks.

q: Which of the following is NOT one of the older, localised banks that can be seen as early differentiated banks?
explain: UCBs, PACS, RRBs and Local Area Banks work in localised areas; SBI is a nationwide public sector bank.

q: Which among the following was the first payments bank of India to start services?
explain: Airtel launched the first payments bank service in India, starting in Rajasthan in 2017. IPPB came later, in September 2018.

q: In September 2015 RBI granted in-principle approval for setting up how many small finance banks?
explain: RBI gave in-principle approval to 10 entities for small finance banks in September 2015.

q: The headquarters of Jana Small Finance Bank Limited is in which city?
explain: Jana Small Finance Bank (started 2018) is headquartered in Bengaluru, like Ujjivan and Fincare.

q: Where is the headquarters of Equitas Small Finance Bank?
explain: Equitas Small Finance Bank is headquartered in Chennai, Tamil Nadu. Thrissur is the home of ESAF.

q: Which city is the headquarters of Capital Small Finance Bank?
explain: Capital Small Finance Bank is based in Jalandhar, Punjab.

q: The headquarters of Utkarsh Small Finance Bank is located in which city?
explain: Utkarsh Small Finance Bank is headquartered in Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh.

q: Which was the first urban co-operative bank to transition into a small finance bank under the voluntary transition scheme?
explain: Shivalik Mercantile Co-operative Bank became Shivalik Small Finance Bank (Noida), listed with a 2021 start.

q: Which pair of small finance banks is listed with 2021 as the year of starting operations?
explain: Shivalik (Noida) and Unity (New Delhi) are the 2021 entrants; Capital and Equitas started in 2016.

q: Which of the following is NOT a payments bank?
explain: Equitas is a small finance bank; Jio, Fino and NSDL operate as payments banks.

q: Which of the following is NOT a small finance bank?
explain: Fino Payments Bank is a payments bank; the other three are small finance banks.

q: Under the original licensing guidelines, the minimum paid-up equity capital for a small finance bank was:
explain: The original norm was ₹100 crore of paid-up equity (later licensing rounds have revised capital norms).

q: Small finance banks must extend what share of their Adjusted Net Bank Credit (ANBC) to priority sector lending?
explain: SFBs must lend 75% of ANBC to priority-sector-eligible segments, higher than the 40% target for other banks.

q: Which loan-portfolio requirement applies to small finance banks?
options: At least 25% of loans up to ₹50 lakh
At least 75% of loans up to ₹25 lakh
At least 40% of loans up to ₹10 lakh
At least 50% of loans up to ₹25 lakh
explain: At least half of an SFB’s loan book must be loans and advances of up to ₹25 lakh.

q: What is the promoter’s minimum initial stake rule for a small finance bank?
explain: The SFB promoter holds at least 40% initially and brings it down to 26% within 12 years. The 15% figure belongs to NOFHCs of new private banks.

q: Which of the following is NOT permitted to a small finance bank?
options: Setting up subsidiaries for non-banking activities
explain: SFBs cannot set up subsidiaries for non-banking activities, but they may sell forex, distribute mutual funds and insurance, and convert into full banks.

q: Which is a recognised challenge for small finance banks?
options: Higher cost of mobilising deposits in rural and underserved areas
A ban on lending to small farmers
A cap of one branch per district
explain: Serving rural and underserved segments makes deposit mobilisation costlier for SFBs.

q: What is the minimum capital requirement for a payments bank?
explain: A payments bank needs ₹100 crore minimum paid-up equity capital.

q: Which of the following does NOT fall within the functions of payments banks?
explain: Payments banks cannot lend; they accept demand deposits, offer remittances and internet banking.

q: Which activity is NOT permitted to payments banks?
explain: Payments banks can issue ATM/debit cards but not credit cards.

q: At least what percentage of a payments bank’s demand deposit balances must be invested in government securities or T-bills?
explain: A minimum of 75% goes into government securities/T-bills; the rest (maximum 25%) can sit with other scheduled commercial banks.

q: What is the maximum share of its funds a payments bank may hold in current and time deposits with other scheduled commercial banks?
explain: The cap is 25%, the mirror image of the 75% minimum in government securities.

q: After RBI raised the limit in 2021, a payments bank can hold demand deposits up to what amount per individual customer?
explain: The per-customer limit was originally ₹1 lakh and was raised to ₹2 lakh.

q: Which of the following can a payments bank NOT do?
options: Act as business correspondent of another bank
explain: Payments banks cannot accept NRI deposits, offer credit cards, lend or handle cross-border remittances.

q: What is a major challenge for payments banks?
options: Their lending book is too large
Low revenue because they cannot lend
They must meet 100% priority sector lending
explain: With no lending, income initially comes only from remittance charges and efficient operations, so revenue is low.

q: Which statement correctly contrasts small finance banks with payments banks?
options: Payments banks can lend to small farmers but SFBs cannot
SFBs can lend but payments banks cannot
explain: SFBs combine deposits and small-ticket lending; payments banks accept deposits and offer payments but cannot lend.

q: India Post Payments Bank was launched by PM Narendra Modi on which date?
explain: IPPB was launched on 1 September 2018 to take banking to people’s doorsteps.

q: India Post Payments Bank is:
options: A joint venture with a telecom operator
A wholly government-owned entity under the Department of Posts
explain: IPPB is a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Department of Posts with 100% Government of India equity, and it is governed by RBI.

q: Which Nobel Prize winner pioneered micro-finance?
explain: Muhammad Yunus pioneered micro-finance, giving the poor capital to start businesses.

q: In India, all loans below what amount can be considered micro-loans?
explain: Loans below ₹1 lakh are treated as micro-loans.

q: A bank’s financial assistance of ₹10,000 to a small borrower will be called:
explain: Very small loans to low-income borrowers fall under micro finance (loans below ₹1 lakh).

q: The Joint Liability Group (JLG) concept for micro-finance was started by which body, and how many members does a JLG have?
explain: NABARD started the JLG concept; a JLG has 4-10 small farmers or rural entrepreneurs from the same locality.

q: Which group is a savings-oriented group of small entrepreneurs who pool a common fund for emergency business needs?
explain: A Self Help Group (SHG) is savings-oriented; a JLG is activity-oriented and focused on income generation.

q: The Local Area Bank Scheme was introduced in which year?
explain: The scheme began in August 1996 following Finance Minister P. Chidambaram’s budget speech.

q: What is the minimum paid-up capital to set up a Local Area Bank?
explain: A Local Area Bank requires minimum paid-up capital of ₹5 crore.

q: A Local Area Bank typically has jurisdiction over:
explain: LABs cover two or three contiguous districts and mobilise rural savings for productive rural uses.

q: Which statement about mutual banking is correct?
options: It is owned by shareholders who buy capital stock
It is owned by its members and has no capital stock
It is owned by the government
It is owned by foreign banks
explain: A mutual bank is owned by members who subscribe to a common fund and share profits and losses; it has no capital stock.

q: Which practice is prohibited under Islamic banking?
explain: Islamic banking forbids collecting or paying interest and relies on profit-and-loss sharing.

q: Which bank, founded in 1975, is regarded as the world’s first full-fledged Islamic bank?
explain: Dubai Islamic Bank, founded in 1975, is described as the first full-fledged Islamic bank in the world.

q: Under RBI’s February 2013 norms, a new private bank’s NOFHC must initially hold at least what share of paid-up voting equity?
explain: The NOFHC holds at least 40%, locked in for five years, and brings it down to 15% within 12 years.

q: What is the initial minimum paid-up voting equity capital for a new private bank under the 2013 guidelines?
explain: The norm was ₹5 billion, i.e. ₹500 crore.

q: Under the 2013 new-bank norms, what share of branches must be in unbanked rural areas (population up to 9,999)?
explain: At least 25% of branches must open in unbanked rural centres; the PSL target for the bank is 40%.

q: Minors above what age are allowed to open and operate savings bank accounts independently as per RBI guidelines?
explain: Minors who have attained 10 years of age can operate savings accounts independently, with ATM and cheque facilities.

q: RuPay, the domestic card payment network, was launched by which body?
explain: RuPay was launched by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI).

q: The Mobile Money Identification Number (MMID) is a number of how many digits, of which the first four identify the bank offering IMPS?
explain: MMID is a 7-digit number whose first four digits identify the bank.

q: Which system powers multiple bank accounts into a single mobile application and merges seamless fund routing and merchant payments?
explain: The Unified Payments Interface (UPI) lets one app hold several bank accounts and route payments instantly.

q: Bharat QR, a common QR-code system for merchant payments, was launched by:
explain: NPCI launched Bharat QR for payments across merchant outlets.

q: Which bank launched its Multi Option Payment Acceptance Device (MOPAD) for digital payments?
explain: MOPAD is an SBI device that accepts several kinds of digital payment.

q: What does BHIM stand for?
explain: BHIM is Bharat Interface for Money, a UPI-based payment app.

q: Banks finalised an inter-creditor agreement under Project Sashakt to resolve the issue of mounting:
explain: Project Sashakt deals with resolving stressed assets, i.e. non-performing assets (NPAs).

q: Which institution was established mainly to promote the Micro, Small and Medium industrial sector in India?
explain: SIDBI (Small Industries Development Bank of India) promotes and finances the MSME sector; NABARD focuses on agriculture and rural development.

q: Allahabad Bank was merged with which of the following banks?
explain: Allahabad Bank was amalgamated into Indian Bank (effective 1 April 2020).

q: The World Bank arm set up in 1960 to provide interest-free loans and grants to the poorest countries is:
explain: IDA helps the world’s poorest countries with zero-interest credits and grants.

q: The National Asset Reconstruction Company Ltd (NARCL), set up in 2021, is popularly known as:
explain: NARCL is called the bad bank because it takes over stressed assets of commercial banks.

q: Which of the following is NOT a regulatory body?
explain: SIDBI is a development finance institution; RBI, SEBI and CCI are regulators.

q: RBI’s regulatory framework for categorising Urban Co-operative Banks has how many tiers?
explain: RBI introduced a four-tiered regulatory framework for UCBs, with norms on net worth and capital adequacy.

q: A savings or current account is treated as inoperative if there are no customer-initiated transactions for how long?
explain: Accounts with no transactions for two years are classed as inoperative/dormant and segregated in separate ledgers.
